section_summary: The section opens with the final panels of a Japanese map of Southern Ocean whaling grounds. The remaining documents concern Allied objections to SCAP’s authorization of a Japanese Antarctic whaling expedition for the 1946–47 season. British, Norwegian, Australian and New Zealand representatives question consultation, security, crews and the precedent for future whaling; State Department and SCAP responses defend the expedition as a supervised, one-season emergency measure.

people.name: John Carter Vincent
people.role: State Department Far Eastern Affairs official

people.name: J. K. Penfield
people.role: Deputy Director, Office of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: Knut Lykke
people.role: Counselor and chargé d’affaires, Norwegian Embassy

people.name: Hugh Beotai
people.role: Recipient named in a handwritten note; name uncertain

people.name: Lavs .Joutad
people.role: Norwegian chargé d’affaires ad interim; signature reading uncertain

subfiles.title: Map of Southern Ocean whaling grounds
subfiles.about: Map panels show Antarctic sectors and Japanese whaling symbols.
subfiles.summary: Final panels of a Japanese map chart Antarctic waters, whale species and catch ranges; its first panel precedes this section.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire on Japanese Antarctic whaling
subfiles.about: Britain protests the expedition and proposes safeguards.
subfiles.summary: Britain asks for Allied control, inspectors, whale quotas and international allocation of all oil. It objects to a tanker conversion that could enable future Japanese whaling.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The United States defends the expedition and responds to British safeguards.
subfiles.summary: The reply calls the expedition a one-season emergency measure under SCAP authority. It promises international compliance, oil allocation and places for additional Allied inspectors, but rejects Allied crews and factory-ship quotas as impractical. Future operations and disposal of equipment remain subject to Allied consultation.

subfiles.title: Conversation with New Zealand representative on whaling
subfiles.about: New Zealand generally supports the British protest but questions some proposed safeguards.
subfiles.summary: Powles reports New Zealand’s qualified support for Britain and offers limited technical personnel.

subfiles.title: Memorandum of conversation concerning Antarctic whaling area
subfiles.about: An OCR-damaged memorandum discusses the geographic area authorized for Japanese whaling.
subfiles.summary: The surviving text quotes the SCAP directive’s Antarctic operating limits and discusses their relation to territorial sectors.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Norwegian Embassy counselor
subfiles.about: Norway presents objections to parts of the British whaling proposal.
subfiles.summary: Lykke says Norway rejects mixed Japanese crews, Japanese flags and factory-ship catch limits.

subfiles.title: Norwegian aide-mémoire on crews and quotas
subfiles.about: Norway clarifies its refusal to staff mixed-crewed ships and its opposition to quotas.
subfiles.summary: Norway will supply no officers for ships with Japanese crew members or a Japanese flag and says international conventions provide no factory-ship quota.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-119 forwarding British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The Department forwards the full British protest to Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Airgram A-119 reproduces Britain’s September 3 aide-mémoire and its proposed safeguards.

subfiles.title: Telegram seeking SCAP assurance on future consultation
subfiles.about: The Department seeks agreement to consult governments before future expeditions.
subfiles.summary: Washington reports Allied protests and asks SCAP to approve a pledge of prior consultation on future whaling.

subfiles.title: Telegram requesting SCAP’s response to Allied objections
subfiles.about: The Department lists foreign objections and requests facts for replies.
subfiles.summary: Washington asks about regulations, security, equipment, tanker conversion, inspection and catch reporting before answering protesting governments.

subfiles.title: Background airgram on Japanese Antarctic whaling controversy
subfiles.about: A confidential circular summarizes the authorization and foreign objections.
subfiles.summary: The Department recounts SCAP’s request and authorization, press disclosure and protests from Norway, Australia, New Zealand and Britain.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram on political consequences of reversal
subfiles.about: Tokyo argues that reversing authorization would damage American authority in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Telegram 404 stresses that Japanese observers see the expedition as an American-approved food measure and warns against reversing it.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: A white telegram copy replaces an unreturned yellow action copy.
subfiles.summary: Record-copy filing notice.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 406 responding to Allied objections
subfiles.about: SCAP staff rebut objections and detail planned controls.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo defends SCAP’s authority and promises compliance, inspections, catch reports and oil allocation. It emphasizes Japanese food needs, describes converted vessels and distinguishes a later tanker conversion from the coming expedition.

subfiles.title: Action copy of Tokyo telegram 406
subfiles.about: A second filed copy repeats Tokyo’s response to Allied objections.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate action copy of telegram 406 concerning controls, food needs and the expedition’s vessels.

subfiles.title: Note on Acheson circulation
subfiles.about: The note questions whether Acheson saw an enclosed paper.
subfiles.summary: Records that the paper came from Acheson’s office without evidence he saw it.

subfiles.title: Vincent memorandum for Acheson on Australian representations
subfiles.about: Vincent supplies Australian correspondence and updates SCAP’s flag and inspector plans.
subfiles.summary: Notes a special flag, one American observer and room for two additional Allied observers per factory ship.

subfiles.title: Australian aide-mémoire on Japanese whaling
subfiles.about: Australia protests authorization and requests an Allied-crewed expedition.
subfiles.summary: Australia objects to the lack of consultation, security implications and possible precedent. It seeks cancellation of the tanker conversion, Allied crews and consideration of a longer prohibition.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Lykke on Norway’s categorical protest
subfiles.about: Lykke delivers Norway’s formal protest and explains concern over precedent.
subfiles.summary: Penfield reports that Lykke chiefly fears revived Japanese whaling capacity and trained personnel, including possible service to other powers.

subfiles.title: Norwegian letter protesting Japanese expedition
subfiles.about: Norway withdraws its fallback proposal for Norwegian operation and demands cancellation.
subfiles.summary: Norway says the season is too close to organize alternative crews and formally protests any Japanese expedition.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Norwegian protest
subfiles.about: The United States asks Norway to withdraw its objections.
subfiles.summary: The reply presents the expedition as a lawful, one-season emergency measure under Allied control. It promises treaty compliance, oil allocation and inspector places, while explaining why Allied crews are impractical and reserving future whaling and reparations for Allied decision.

subfiles.title: Correction of expedition flag designation
subfiles.about: The Department corrects the flag description in its October 16 note.
subfiles.summary: Corrects SCAJAP flag “O” to “E” and notes planned international and local notification.

subfiles.title: Message authorizing SCAJAP flag E
subfiles.about: Washington authorizes flag E and requests local notice.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes SCAJAP flag E for whaling and asks SCAP to promulgate its use locally.

subfiles.title: SCAP inquiry on weekly whale catch statistics
subfiles.about: SCAP asks how to transmit required factory-ship catch statistics.
subfiles.summary: Requests the reporting route and address for weekly blue-whale-unit statistics.

subfiles.title: Department reply on reporting, observers and biological work
subfiles.about: Washington directs reporting and asks for inspection and scientific details.
subfiles.summary: The Department directs catch reports to Sandefjord, presses for Allied inspectors and a special flag, and requests enforcement and biological data.

subfiles.title: SCAP assurance that authorization is limited to one season
subfiles.about: SCAP reiterates Allied control and the expedition’s temporary authorization.
subfiles.summary: Tokyo says the expedition is a one-season emergency measure and that SCAP plans no action beyond U.S. authorization.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-129 forwarding New Zealand aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The Department forwards New Zealand’s August 23 objections.
subfiles.summary: New Zealand cites proximity, security, Japan’s past whaling record and lack of consultation, and suggests an Allied operation.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-130 forwarding Norwegian aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Norway’s September 6 position.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces Norway’s refusal to staff mixed-crewed ships and its objection to factory-ship quotas.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-131 forwarding Australian aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Australia’s September 16 protest.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces Australia’s requests for consultation, cancellation of tanker conversion, Allied crews and consideration of prohibiting Japanese Antarctic whaling.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-133 forwarding Norwegian categorical protest
subfiles.about: The Department forwards Norway’s demand that the expedition be cancelled.
subfiles.summary: Reproduces Norway’s September 17 letter withdrawing its alternative crew proposal and protesting the planned expedition.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Australian aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: The Department begins its response to Australia’s objections.
subfiles.summary: The surviving portion argues that SCAP acted within an existing directive, that the expedition addresses oil and food shortages, and that inspectors will ensure compliance. It also rejects the claim that the 1945 conference resolution is violated; the document continues beyond page 397.
